source_refs.note: Topic 2.10 with Fig. 2.16 and Example 2.10 (PDF 45-46, 50; printed 42-43, 47).

blocks.text: Consider two bodies of masses m1 and m2 moving with velocities v1i and v2i along the same line, with v1i greater than v2i, so that m1 is regarded as the projectile and m2 as the target. After time t the bodies make an inelastic collision and stick together; their combined mass m1 + m2 moves with final velocity vf after the collision (Fig. 2.16). Since the collision is perfectly inelastic, the total momentum is conserved: total momentum before = total momentum after, m1 v1i + m2 v2i = (m1 + m2) vf, so vf = (m1/(m1 + m2)) v1i + (m2/(m1 + m2)) v2i, the common velocity of the body after the inelastic collision. In the special case when the target m2 is at rest, v2i = 0, vf = (m1/(m1 + m2)) v1i ... (2.37): the velocity of m1 is reduced by the mass ratio m1/(m1 + m2); the larger the mass of m1, the faster the combination moves.

The system's kinetic energy before the collision is (KE)i = (1/2) m1 v1i^2 + (1/2) m2 v2i^2, and the kinetic energy of the combination after the collision is (KE)f = (1/2)(m1 + m2) vf^2. The fraction of kinetic energy lost is ((KE)i - (KE)f)/(KE)i = ([(1/2) m1 v1i^2 + (1/2) m2 v2i^2] - (1/2)(m1 + m2) vf^2) / [(1/2) m1 v1i^2 + (1/2) m2 v2i^2]. Putting the value of vf from (2.37) and taking the special case of a target at rest (v2i = 0), solving gives ((KE)i - (KE)f)/(KE)i = m2/(m1 + m2) ... (2.38). This is the fraction of kinetic energy lost during the inelastic collision; energy is lost during an inelastic collision in one dimension.

blocks.title: Example 2.10 (printed after 2.12)
blocks.text: A projectile of mass 2 kg moving with initial velocity 4 m s^-1 towards the right hits a target at rest of mass 3 kg; after the collision the two masses stick together and move as a single body with velocity 1.6 m s^-1. Show the law of conservation of momentum and the energy loss during the perfectly inelastic collision. Solution: initial momentum in the x-direction p = m1 v1i + m2 v2i = (2 kg x 4 m s^-1) + (3 kg x 0) = 8 kg m s^-1 (v2i = 0). The combined mass is M = m1 + m2 = 2 kg + 3 kg = 5 kg and vf = 1.6 m s^-1, so the final momentum is M vf = 5 kg x 1.6 m s^-1 = 8 kg m s^-1. Initial KE = (1/2) x 2 kg x (4 m s^-1)^2 + (1/2) x 3 kg x 0 = 16 J; final KE = (1/2)(m1 + m2) vf^2 = (1/2) x 5 kg x (1.6 m s^-1)^2 = 6.4 J; energy loss = 16 J - 6.4 J = 9.6 J. Momentum is conserved but kinetic energy is lost.

blocks.explanation: vf = m1 v1i/(m1 + m2) = 2 x 4/5 = 1.6 m s^-1, as given. The fraction lost should be m2/(m1 + m2) = 3/5 = 0.6, and indeed 9.6 J / 16 J = 0.6.

items: Perfectly inelastic: bodies stick; momentum conserved, m1 v1i + m2 v2i = (m1 + m2) vf; target at rest: vf = m1 v1i/(m1 + m2) and the fraction of KE lost is m2/(m1 + m2). Example 2.10: 8 kg m s^-1 before and after, 9.6 J of 16 J lost.
